_comment: The 23 Cisco content modules. Titles reconstructed from the public Networking Basics scope (see cisco-module-map.md). Confirm against the coach course. `strand` is the module's primary spiral strand and drives its colour. `explainer` true means content/module-NN.html exists.

modules.title: Communication in a Connected World
modules.summary: What a network is for, and the three roles every device on one plays: host, client, server.
objectives: Explain the purpose of a computer network
Distinguish hosts, clients, and servers, and explain why one device can be more than one of them
Describe how a LAN relates to the Internet
modules.watchfor: Vocabulary questions. 'Client' and 'server' are roles, not hardware. The quiz likes that distinction.

modules.title: Network Components, Types, and Connections
modules.summary: Every icon in the Packet Tracer device bar, what it does, and how to read a network diagram.
objectives: Distinguish end devices from intermediary devices
Identify switches, routers, access points, modems, and NICs by icon and by function
Recognize LAN vs. WAN and read a basic network diagram
Distinguish logical from physical topology
modules.watchfor: Given a described requirement, pick the right device. Switch vs. router is the most common trap. A switch does not connect different networks.

modules.title: Wireless and Mobile Networks
modules.summary: Wi-Fi and cellular: how a client finds an AP, what an SSID actually is, and the wireless security ladder.
objectives: Explain how wireless clients associate with an access point
Describe the role of the SSID and what hiding it does and does not accomplish
Order the wireless security standards and name the current best practice
Distinguish Wi-Fi from cellular and Bluetooth by range and use case
modules.watchfor: The security ordering WEP < WPA < WPA2 < WPA3 is near-guaranteed. Know that SSID hiding and MAC filtering are speed bumps, not controls.

modules.title: Build a Home Network
modules.summary: The integrated wireless router: the one box that is a router, a switch, an AP, and a DHCP server at the same time.
objectives: Identify the WAN port and the LAN ports on an integrated wireless router and explain why they are different
Configure an SSID and WPA2/WPA3 security
Configure the LAN-side DHCP scope
Explain why changing the default admin credentials is the first step, not the last
modules.watchfor: Configuration-order questions. The WAN port faces the ISP; the LAN ports and the wireless side are the same network.

modules.title: Communication Principles
modules.summary: Protocols, standards, and the two models, OSI and TCP/IP, plus encapsulation, which is the idea the whole course rests on.
objectives: Explain what a protocol is and why standards exist
Name the OSI layers in order and map the four-layer TCP/IP model onto them
Trace encapsulation and de-encapsulation across a network
Name the PDU at each layer: data, segment, packet, frame, bits
modules.watchfor: Layer-order recall and PDU naming. Expect 'at which layer does X happen' and 'what is the PDU called at layer N'.

modules.title: Network Media
modules.summary: Copper, fiber, and wireless: what each is good at, what breaks it, and how to pick one from a scenario.
objectives: Identify UTP, STP, coaxial, fiber, and wireless media and their connectors
Compare media by bandwidth, distance, cost, and interference susceptibility
Select the right media for a stated scenario
Explain attenuation, EMI, and crosstalk
modules.watchfor: Scenario-to-media questions: long run, electrically noisy factory floor, or between buildings. That is fiber every time.

modules.title: The Access Layer
modules.summary: The Ethernet frame, the MAC address, and how a switch learns where everything is.
objectives: Describe the fields of an Ethernet frame and the structure of a MAC address
Explain how a switch builds its MAC address table from source addresses
Predict whether a switch will forward, flood, or filter a given frame
Explain broadcasts and the scope of a broadcast domain
modules.watchfor: Given a MAC table and an incoming frame, what does the switch do? This is the archetypal conceptual-application question.

modules.title: The Internet Protocol
modules.summary: What an IP address is, how the mask splits it, and why Layer 2 and Layer 3 addressing both have to exist.
objectives: Explain the purpose of an IP address and the structure of IPv4
Separate the network portion from the host portion given any subnet mask
Express a mask in dotted-decimal and CIDR notation interchangeably
Distinguish MAC addressing from IP addressing and say when each is used
modules.watchfor: Mask-to-CIDR conversion has to be instant. /24 = 255.255.255.0 should not require thought.

modules.title: IPv4 and Network Segmentation
modules.summary: Address types, reserved ranges, and the question everything else depends on: are these two hosts on the same network?
objectives: Distinguish unicast, multicast, and broadcast traffic
Identify private (RFC 1918), public, loopback, link-local/APIPA, and multicast ranges
Determine whether two hosts are on the same subnet
Explain the consequence when they are not
modules.watchfor: 169.254.x.x means DHCP failed. That is a diagnostic fact, not trivia. Know the three private ranges cold.

modules.title: IPv6 Addressing Formats and Rules
modules.summary: 128 bits in hex, the two compression rules, and how to tell an address type at a glance.
objectives: Read, compress, and expand IPv6 addresses correctly
Identify global unicast, link-local, and multicast addresses by prefix
Configure IPv6 addressing on hosts and router interfaces
Explain dual stack
modules.watchfor: The :: can appear only once in an address. Compression questions are free points if you know both rules.

modules.title: Dynamic Addressing with DHCP
modules.summary: DORA, the pool, and what a client is actually handed besides an address.
objectives: Explain DHCP operation and trace the DORA exchange
Compare static and dynamic addressing and say when each is correct
Configure a DHCP pool with gateway and DNS information
Verify a client lease
modules.watchfor: DORA order, and what a rogue DHCP server can do to a network that trusts any offer it receives.

modules.title: Gateways to Other Networks
modules.summary: The default gateway: what a host does when the destination is not local, and what happens when the gateway is wrong.
objectives: Explain the role of the default gateway in packet forwarding
Describe routers as network boundaries
Explain the failure mode when a gateway is missing or wrong
Explain what NAT does in a small network, conceptually
modules.watchfor: 'Can ping local hosts but nothing outside' is a gateway question, every time.

modules.title: The ARP Process
modules.summary: How a host turns an IP address into a MAC address, and why it ARPs for the gateway, not the far host.
objectives: Explain ARP request broadcast and unicast reply
Read an ARP cache and explain aging and clearing
Explain how ARP behaves differently for local vs. remote destinations
Relate ARP to the switch's MAC address table
modules.watchfor: The signature idea: for a remote destination you ARP for your gateway's MAC, not the destination host's.

modules.title: Routing Between Networks
modules.summary: The routing table: what is in it, where entries come from, and how the router picks one.
objectives: Explain why a router is required for communication between networks
Read a routing table: directly connected, static, and default entries
Configure static and default routes and prove reachability
Diagnose a route that exists but does not work, usually a missing return route
modules.watchfor: A one-way ping failure is almost always a missing return route. Routing is symmetric or it is broken.

modules.title: TCP and UDP
modules.summary: The transport layer: reliability versus speed, ports and sockets, and the numbers you have to know cold.
objectives: Distinguish TCP from UDP by behavior and by use case
Explain ports and sockets
Recall the well-known port numbers on demand
Explain the three-way handshake, acknowledgment, and sequencing
modules.watchfor: 20/21 FTP · 22 SSH · 23 Telnet · 25 SMTP · 53 DNS · 67/68 DHCP · 69 TFTP · 80 HTTP · 110 POP3 · 143 IMAP · 443 HTTPS. Memorize these.

modules.title: Application Layer Services
modules.summary: DNS, HTTP, email, and FTP: configuring them on a Packet Tracer server and tracing what a client actually does.
objectives: Explain and configure DNS, HTTP/HTTPS, email, FTP, and DHCP on a Packet Tracer server
Trace a name-to-address resolution end to end
Describe the client/server model at the application layer
Explain why a DNS failure looks like a connectivity failure to a user
modules.watchfor: 'Ping by IP works, ping by name fails' is DNS. That single symptom pair shows up constantly.

modules.title: Network Testing Utilities
modules.summary: The tools, what each one actually proves, and the fixed order you run them in.
objectives: Use ping, tracert/traceroute, ipconfig, ifconfig/ip, and nslookup correctly
State what each utility proves and what it does not
Isolate a fault by layer and narrate the reasoning
Execute the standard diagnostic sequence without prompting
modules.watchfor: Diagnose systematically instead of randomly changing settings. Expect 'which command would you run next' questions.

modules.title: Network Design
modules.summary: Hierarchical design, redundancy, and choosing devices to meet a stated requirement instead of a habit.
objectives: Explain hierarchical network design and the access/distribution/core roles
Explain reliability, scalability, redundancy, and fault tolerance
Select devices and topology to meet a stated requirement
Explain quality-of-service considerations at a basic level
modules.watchfor: Requirement-to-design questions. Redundancy means no single failure takes the network down. Name the single point of failure.

modules.title: Cloud and Virtualization
modules.summary: Virtual machines, virtual networks, and where the line between local and cloud actually sits.
objectives: Explain virtual machines and the role of a hypervisor
Describe virtual networks and data centers
Distinguish the cloud service models
Distinguish local from cloud resources in a given scenario
modules.watchfor: Service-model sorting: who manages what. SaaS you use, PaaS you build on, IaaS you run.

modules.title: Number Systems
modules.summary: Binary, decimal, and hex conversion: the prerequisite skill for Module 23 and the whole Semifinals.
objectives: Convert fluently between binary, decimal, and hexadecimal
Express any IPv4 address and mask in binary
Express MAC and IPv6 values in hex
Perform binary ANDing to derive a network address
modules.watchfor: Speed matters more than method. 128 64 32 16 8 4 2 1 should be automatic.

modules.title: Ethernet Switching
modules.summary: The switch forwarding decision in depth: the deep-dive counterpart to Module 7. Unlocks at Round 2.
objectives: Walk the full switch forwarding decision: learn source, look up destination, then forward, flood, or filter
Explain MAC table aging and what a table miss produces
Predict switch behavior for a given frame and table state
Relate collision domains and broadcast domains to switch ports
modules.watchfor: Out of numeric order. This unlocks at Round 2, before Modules 12–17. Do not skip it waiting for its number to come up.

modules.title: Network Layer
modules.summary: How a router forwards a packet, what the headers carry, and the one fact that ties the whole course together.
objectives: Describe Layer 3 operation and the fields of an IPv4 and an IPv6 packet header
Explain host forwarding logic: local or remote, and what happens in each case
Trace a packet across a router boundary
Name what changes at each hop (MAC addresses) and what does not (IP addresses)
modules.watchfor: The signature lesson: across a routed path, Layer 2 addresses are rewritten at every hop while Layer 3 addresses stay the same end to end.

modules.title: IPv4 Address Structure
modules.summary: Subnetting. The highest-value skill in the Semifinals, and the most common place points are lost.
objectives: Perform binary ANDing to derive a network address
Given a network and prefix, produce every subnet: network address, first and last usable host, broadcast address, and usable host count
Choose an appropriate subnet size for a stated host requirement
Convert between dotted-decimal mask and CIDR prefix instantly
modules.watchfor: Produce on demand: mask, prefix, network, broadcast, first host, last host, host count, and the right subnet size for a requirement.
